turns.prompt_text: I am going to purchase a GM washer drier 2 in 1,
turns.response_html:
Buying a GE Profile UltraFast Combo (the 2-in-1 unit) is a major shift in how you’ll do laundry. Based on a wide range of perspectives—from appliance technicians and busy families to eco-conscious apartment dwellers—here is an integrated look at what you can expect.

1. The Lifestyle Shift: "Set and Forget"

The biggest praise for this machine comes from people who value mental bandwidth.

  • The Busy Professional/Parent: Many users report that it "removes the laundry tax"—the stress of forgetting wet clothes in the washer until they smell. You can start a load at 10:00 PM and wake up to dry clothes.
  • The Single User/Small Household: For those who live alone or in small apartments, this is often called "life-changing" because it eliminates the need for a 240V outlet or external venting.
  • The "Mountain of Laundry" Reality: If you have a family of five and do 10+ loads a week, this machine can be a bottleneck. Since you can't wash a second load while the first is drying, your throughput is slower than a traditional "side-by-side" set.

2. Technical Performance: Heat Pump vs. Heating Element

Unlike traditional dryers that use a glowing red heating element, this unit uses Heat Pump Technology.

  • Efficiency: It uses about 50% less energy and is much gentler on fabrics because it dries at lower temperatures.
  • The "Damp" Sensation: A common "pro-tip" from the community: when the cycle finishes, clothes may feel slightly humid to the touch due to the sealed drum. However, if you take them out and give them a quick shake, the moisture evaporates instantly.
  • Speed: Despite the "UltraFast" name, a full load of towels or heavy jeans will still take 2 to 3 hours to go from dirty to dry.

3. Maintenance: The "Hidden" Work

Technicians and long-term owners emphasize that because this is a complex 2-in-1, it requires more "active" maintenance than a standard washer.

  • The Lint Challenge: It has a unique two-stage filter. You must clean this every single load. Some users have reported lint bypassing the filter and gunking up the internal "fins" (the heat exchanger), which can eventually lead to longer dry times or service calls.
  • Software Updates: Because it's a smart appliance, keeping it connected to Wi-Fi is actually important. GE frequently pushes "over-the-air" updates that recalibrate the drying sensors based on real-world data from other users.

4. Comparison Summary

FeatureGE Profile 2-in-1Traditional Separate Set
Installation120V Standard Plug (No Vent)240V Heavy Duty + Vent
ConvenienceHigh (No load transfer)Low (Must move wet clothes)
Speed2–3 hours total~1.5 hours total (parallel)
Fabric CareHigh (Gentle heat pump)Medium (High heat can shrink)

💡 Recommendation & Tips

If you decide to go through with the purchase:

  1. Buy the Riser: The unit is low to the ground. Unless you're very comfortable bending over, the optional pedestal makes a big difference for your back.
  2. Use Less Detergent: This machine is highly efficient. Using too much soap (a common habit from old top-loaders) can cause suds to leak or build up in the internal sensors.
  3. The "Morning Fold" Routine: Adopt a rhythm of starting a load right before bed. It removes the "waiting for the dryer" frustration entirely.

The GE Profile UltraFast Combo (PFQ97HSPVDS) is a highly-rated, all-in-one laundry solution that has gained a reputation for its speed and energy efficiency. It is currently available at major retailers, often at a significant discount from its $2,999 list price.

Product Overview

The GE Profile PFQ97HSPVDS is designed to wash and dry a full load in roughly two hours. It uses a ventless heat pump, which means it doesn't require an external exhaust vent and can be plugged into a standard 120V outlet.

  • Capacity: 4.8 cu. ft. (large enough for a king-size comforter).
  • Key Features: Adaptive SmartDispense (holds up to 32 loads of detergent), Microban antimicrobial technology on the gasket and dispenser, and Pet Hair Removal cycle.
  • Installation: Ventless design allows for flexible placement in closets or bathrooms.
  • Efficiency: ENERGY STAR certified; uses up to 50% less energy than a standard vented dryer.

Current Market Pricing & Availability

As of December 2025, you can find this model at several major appliance retailers. Prices typically range from $1,849 to $2,099 depending on active holiday promotions.

  • Best Buy: Frequently offers this model at a sale price around $2,099. They also stock the 4.6 cu. ft. White version (PFQ83HSSWWW) if you prefer a different finish.
  • The Home Depot: Lists the unit with options for professional installation and haul-away services.
  • Specialty Retailers: Sites like Airport Appliance have recently listed it as low as $1,849.

What Users are Saying

  • Pros: Owners frequently praise how quiet the machine is and the convenience of not having to "switch" laundry. Many "natural learners" who value efficiency note that it simplifies their daily rhythm significantly.
  • Cons: Some users mention that extremely heavy loads (like several pairs of jeans) may occasionally require an extra 10–15 minutes of drying time. There is also a community of enthusiasts who suggest aftermarket lint filter upgrades for those who want to maximize long-term maintenance.

turns.prompt_text: Would it be difficult to install this washer/dryer myself or should I purchase the installation plan?
turns.response_html:
Whether you should install the GE Profile UltraFast Combo yourself or pay for a plan depends largely on your comfort with moving heavy objects and basic plumbing.

The installation is technically simpler than a traditional set because it is ventless and uses a standard 120V outlet, but there are some physical challenges to consider:

Why You Might Do It Yourself

  • No Venting Required: Since it uses heat pump technology, you don't have to struggle with rigid or semi-rigid aluminum dryer ducts.
  • Standard Power: It plugs into a regular three-prong 120V outlet, so you don't need a specialized 240V "dryer plug" or an electrician.
  • Simple Plumbing: You only need to connect standard hot and cold water hoses and a drain pipe, just like a regular washer.

Why You Should Consider the Installation Plan

  • Extreme Weight: This unit is a single, heavy machine weighing about 302 lbs. Unlike separate units, you are moving the weight of a washer and dryer combined in one chassis.
  • Complexity of Leveling: All-in-one units spin at very high speeds (up to 1,300 RPM). If the machine isn't perfectly level on a stable floor, it can cause significant vibration and noise.
  • Shipping Bolts: You must remember to remove the heavy-duty shipping bolts from the back before use. Professional installers handle this and typically haul away the massive shipping crate and pallet, which can be a hassle to dispose of yourself.

Final Recommendation: If you have at least one strong person to help you move it and you are comfortable using a wrench to level the feet, you can save the money. However, if you are installing this in a tight space or on a second floor, the professional installation plan is worth it just for the heavy lifting and the removal of the packing materials.
